docs.t: 1. Electrical Power Up (SP.6) - Electrical Power Up — read & do
docs.x: 1. Electrical Power Up (SP.6) Electrical Power Up — read & do FCOM SP.6.2 (reference, not drilled) [FCOM SP.6.2 — Electrical Power Up. Supplementary Procedure; read & do for a cold/dark/unpowered airplane. Quoted verbatim, reference only, not a trained flow.] “The following procedure is accomplished to permit safe application of electrical power.” • BATTERY switch — ON • C1 and C2 ELEC pump selectors — OFF • DEMAND pump selectors — OFF • WIPER selectors — OFF • Landing gear lever — DN • ALTN FLAPS selector — OFF • Electrical power — Establish - If external power is desired: EXT PWR AVAIL light(s) — Illuminated; EXT PWR switch(es) — Push - If APU power is desired: APU GENERATOR switches — ON; wait 15 seconds after the left CCR is online; APU selector — START, then ON • Note: the MAIN BATTERY LOW message can show when power is established; the main battery is charging and the message blanks when charge is sufficient for takeoff Goes prior to the Preliminary Preflight Procedure (NP.21.1 assumes Electrical Power Up complete). BOTH

2. Prelim Preflight IRS selectors OFF 30 seconds, then ON [FCOM NP.21.1-2:] • OFF 30 seconds then ON. Verify the ON BAT light is extinguished • The 30-second OFF cycle clears the IRS memory before alignment begins • Assumes Electrical Power Up (SP.6) is complete BOTH

2. Prelim Preflight STATUS / EICAS displays (SYS) Check 3 fluids (HYD, OXY, OIL); CREW OXYGEN LOW blank [FCOM NP.21.1-2:] • Click SYS (STATUS display): verify only expected messages are shown • Check the 3 fluids sufficient for flight: HYD (hydraulic qty), OXY (oxygen pressure), OIL (engine oil qty) - oxygen and hydraulic quantity on the STATUS display; engine oil quantity on the secondary engine display • EICAS display: verify only expected alert and memo messages are shown; unexpected messages require MEL check before dispatch • Ground conditioned air connected: refer to SP.2 • CREW OXYGEN LOW: verify the alert message is blank on EICAS (performed only after a crew change or maintenance action) [FCOM NP.21:] • During preflight, check oxygen mask stowed and door closed • RESET/TEST: push and hold, verify yellow cross in flow indicator, release • Selector to 100%. (FCOM NP.21 Preflight Procedure) BOTH

docs.t: 3. CDU Preflight - CDU build - the page-flow spine
docs.x: 3. CDU Preflight CDU build - the page-flow spine PF builds, page by page (FCOM NP.21.2-5) [Six steps between two datalink bookends. Build it in this order:] • Bookend IN - D-ATIS (press COMM): FLIGHT INFORMATION > ATIS REQUEST. Verify altimeter number = letter (SP.5.1) • 1 INITIAL DATA: IDENT, POS INIT • 2 NAV DATA: RTE, DEPARTURES, POS REF 2, NAV RADIO (engine-out departure), ARRIVALS, FIX INFO (ETOPS) • 3 PERF DATA: PERF INIT - ZFW, fuel agrees, RESERVES, CRZ ALT, COST INDEX, STEP 0 (done before Before Start) • 4 WIND DATA: FMC COMM - WIND, DES FORECAST, CLB FORECAST • 5 LEGS VERIFICATION: LEGS, then NAV DATA via INIT REF > INDEX (independent ARINC 424 lat/long over water) • 6 REGISTER: OPS CONTROL (COMPANY-FLIGHT INIT), ATC LOGIN (KSEA = KUSA, PHNL = clearance) • Bookend OUT - REQUEST preliminary performance (do not load) [LINK:cdu_preflight.html|Open the full CDU page-flow study aid] PF

Before Start Departure Clearance Obtain [FCOM NP.21.26-29:] • FO obtains ATC departure clearance before the Before Start Procedure • Start this procedure after the PREFLIGHT CHECKLIST is complete • Continue once LCO and final takeoff performance data are available [FCTM:] • FCTM Preflight: obtain clearance early to allow time for FMC route changes if the clearance differs from the flight plan FO

docs.x: 6. Before Start Joint Verbal FMC RTE Crosscheck Complete [FCOM NP.21.26-29:] • PF reads the ATC clearance while PM crosschecks against FMC RTE pages and flight plan • PF reads total distance and fuel over destination from PROG 1/4 - PM crosschecks against the flight plan • If ORCN segment waypoints in the departure clearance differ from those on the flight plan or FMC RTE, repeat the dual independent legs verification, total distance and fuel check, and this crosscheck BOTH

docs.t: 6. Before Start - Taxi and Takeoff briefings
docs.x: 6. Before Start Taxi and Takeoff briefings Complete [FCOM NP.21.26-29:] • The pilot who will do the takeoff does both briefings • The taxi briefing covers taxi routing, hot spots, and expected runway • The takeoff briefing covers V-speeds, engine failure procedures, rejected takeoff criteria, and departure routing • Then continue once LCO and final performance data are available [PRC Crew Briefing Card:] • Threats: PM states first, then PF • Plan: Taxi / Departure Runway · Takeoff Performance + Configuration · Route (ATC clearance vs programmed route) · Return (emergency / takeoff alternate) • Considerations: any specific PM duties, recap as needed • FA emergency brief when required - NTSB: Nature of emergency, Time to prepare, Special instructions, Brace signal PF

Before Start LCO Verification Complete [FCOM NP.21.26-29:] • FO reads from the Load Closeout, CA verifies against the Dispatch Release: flight number, UTC date, tail number, and takeoff weight (within FOM Dispatch Release Weight Tolerances) • Then Passenger Count Verification: FO reads passenger count and jumpseat numbers from the Load Closeout - CA verifies against the Flight Deck Report provided in JetPack BOTH

Before Start Passenger Count Verification Perform [FCOM NP.21.27:] • The First Officer reads the passenger count and jumpseat numbers from the Load Closeout • The Captain verifies the numbers match the Flight Deck Report provided in JetPack or via alternate means • Refer to FOM "Passenger Count Verification" BOTH

Note: HA operations do not allow TO 1 or TO 2 BOTH

Unwanted tow bar movement can occur FO

Before Start HYDRAULIC panel Set [FCOM NP.21.29:] • RIGHT ELECTRIC DEMAND pump selector - AUTO (verify FAULT light extinguished) • CENTER 1 and CENTER 2 ELECTRIC pump selectors - AUTO (verify FAULT lights extinguished) • LEFT ELECTRIC DEMAND pump selector - AUTO (verify FAULT light extinguished) FO

Engine Start Secondary engine indications Select [FCOM NP.21.30:] • FO selects the secondary engine indications • Crew action to correct for abnormal engine indications is not needed; respond to any EICAS messages that show • APU is the preferred electric power source for engine start; engines may not start with external power and APU both supplying power • Do not make flap or primary flight control inputs on the ground until the EICAS engine RUNNING indication appears and all four GEN CTRL OFF lights are extinguished • CAUTION: If OAT is above 40°C, do not attempt to start both engines at the same time FO

Engine Start Start clearance Obtain [FCOM NP.21.30-31:] • CA obtains ATC clearance to start engines • The engines may be started at the same time • The engines can only be started using the autostart system • NOTE: engines may not start if external power and APU are both supplying power simultaneously - one source must be selected off • APU is the preferred source [FCOM NP.21.30:] • FCOM NP.21.30: do not make flap or primary flight control inputs on the ground until after the EICAS engine RUNNING indication appears and all four GEN CTRL OFF lights are extinguished • Electric spoilers are susceptible to nuisance failures if commanded during electrical power transfers • Note: unplug portable devices (such as portable EFBs) before engine start to reduce electrical anomalies with the power outlets; plug back in once engines have stabilized CA

Before Taxi Flap lever Set takeoff flaps [FCOM NP.21.31-32:] • CA calls "FLAPS ___", FO sets takeoff flaps • Flaps are set on Captain's command after the pushback escort salute • Cold weather: if taxiing through ice, snow, slush, or standing water at low temperatures, consider delaying flap extension to just before the Before Takeoff Procedure to prevent contamination BOTH

Before Taxi Flight controls Check [FCOM NP.21.31-32:] • CA checks flight controls • Make slow and deliberate inputs, one direction at a time • Control wheel and control column: full travel both directions, verify freedom of movement and return to center • Hold the rudder pedal disconnect switch down during the rudder check to prevent nose wheel movement • Rudder pedals: full travel both directions [FCOM NP.21.31:] • FCOM NP.21.31 Before Taxi Procedure: flight control check confirms no binding, correct surface movement direction, and full travel range • Perform before taxi, not while moving # Avoid rapid and large alternating control inputs, especially in combination with large changes in pitch, roll, or yaw (e.g. large sideslip angles) as they may result in structural failure at any speed, including below VA (FCOM L.10.10) CA

Before Taxi Recall Check [FCOM NP.21.31-32:] • Both pilots recall • Only expected alert and memo messages should be shown • Update the taxi briefing as needed based on any new ATIS, gate hold, or routing • Then CA calls BEFORE TAXI CHECKLIST. This is also the transition point: CA/FO role assignments transition to PF/PM at completion of this checklist ✅ BEFORE TAXI CHECKLIST — CA calls, FO reads, both verify. Before Takeoff WX radar Set as needed [FCOM NP.21.33:] • PF sets WX radar as needed for departure • Update the takeoff briefing if weather or routing has changed • Check the departure corridor for weather, especially any convective activity near the departure airport [FCTM:] • FCTM 3.13: update the takeoff briefing any time weather or routing changes from what was briefed • Sterile flight deck applies below 10,000 ft MSL, except cruise flight (FOM 2.3.12) # Max tailwind for takeoff: 15 kt (FCOM L.10.2) # Avoid weather radar operation in a hangar or near fuel-soaked pavement (test mode exempt) (FCOM L.10.3) # Takeoff is permitted only in the normal flight control mode (FCOM L.10.10) PF

Takeoff Transponder TA/RA entering runway [FCOM NP.21.34-35:] • PM sets transponder to TA/RA mode when entering the runway • Mode change from XPDR to TA/RA enables TCAS traffic advisories and resolution advisories • Per HAL Flows Rev 4 and PRC [FCTM:] • FCTM: setting TA/RA on the runway rather than earlier prevents nuisance TAs from ground traffic at busy airports while ensuring full TCAS protection during the takeoff roll and climb PM

Takeoff ND verification Symbol on assigned rwy, headings agree [FCOM NP.21.34-35:] • When lined up, both pilots verify the aircraft symbol on the ND is on the assigned runway and runway heading agrees • For HUD takeoff: verify ground deviation indications including guidance cue, ground reference cue, and ground excessive deviation symbol [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 3: this is the final cross-check before releasing brakes • Per HAL PRC: "Both Pilots: Visually Verify the Aircraft symbol on ND is on assigned Runway and runway heading agrees." 11. Takeoff LANDING lights ON when cleared for takeoff [FCOM NP.21.34-35:] • PM selects LANDING lights ON when cleared for takeoff • PF: brakes released, thrust levers to approximately 40% N1, allow engines to stabilize, then push TO/GA switch • Verify takeoff thrust • Maximum thrust may not be available until 65 kts • Captain keeps hand on thrust levers until V1 • At 80 kts PM calls "80 Knots," PF calls "Check." At Vr PM calls "Rotate." [FCTM:] • FCTM 3.4: advance levers to ~40% N1 for stabilization, then TO/GA • Nominal all-engine rotation is smooth and continuous toward 15 degrees pitch (FCTM 3.6); with an engine inoperative the target is 12 to 13 degrees (FCTM 3.34) • Do not over-rotate • V1 is the go/no-go decision speed - above V1 the takeoff must continue regardless of failure # HUD takeoff: max headwind 25 kt, max tailwind 15 kt, max crosswind 20 kt (FCOM L.10.9) [Light Switch Positions card, 27MAR24:] [IMG:lights/cleared_for_takeoff.jpg] PM

12. After Takeoff Flaps Retract on schedule (PF calls, PM sets) [FCOM NP.21.36:] • PF calls flap retractions on schedule; PM sets • From flaps 20/18/17/15/10: at the takeoff flap setting select 5, at 5 select 1, at 1 select UP. From 5: at 5 select 1, at 1 select UP. Do not exceed flap placard speeds • Acceleration height is the point where speed is set to the maneuver speed for the planned flap setting [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 3: retract flaps on schedule at acceleration height • Verify CLB thrust is set and the airplane is tracking the departure route before calling the After Takeoff Checklist • Maximum bank 30 degrees is permitted at V2+15 with takeoff flaps for an immediate turn (FCTM 3.30); with an engine out the AFDS itself limits bank to 15 degrees until V2+10 (FCTM 3.37) # Autopilot must not be engaged below 200 ft AGL after takeoff (FCOM L.10.8) PM

12. After Takeoff ENGINE ANTI-ICE selectors AUTO (after retraction complete) [FCOM NP.21.36:] • PM sets ENGINE ANTI-ICE selectors to AUTO after flap retraction is complete • With engines running and in normal flight, the AUTO mode is the standard setting • The anti-ice valves open automatically when the ice detection system detects icing conditions [FCOM Ch 3 Anti-Ice, Rain:] • AUTO: in flight, the engine anti-ice valves are opened or closed automatically by the ice detection system • EAI on AUTO provides automatic protection without pilot workload; not needed during initial climbout in non-icing conditions • Setting it after retraction complete is the standard HAL After Takeoff procedure per FCOM NP.21.36 and the PRC PM

docs.t: 15. Descent - Recall / alert and memo messages
docs.x: 15. Descent Recall / alert and memo messages Review [FCOM NP.21.38-39:] • Start before descending below cruise altitude for arrival - complete by 10,000 ft AFE. PF reviews alert and memo messages and all operational notes • PM independently recalls and reviews both • Any unexpected messages require the applicable NNC # Severe turbulent air penetration speed: below 25,000 ft MSL: 290 KIAS | at/above 25,000 ft MSL: 310 KIAS / .84M, whichever is lower (FCOM L.10.3) # Maximum altitude with flaps extended: 20,000 ft (FCOM L.10.10) BOTH

15. Descent Landing performance / VREF Check, verify/enter on APPROACH REF [FCOM NP.21.38-39:] • PF checks landing performance and verifies VREF - PM enters VREF on the APPROACH REF page • Landing performance includes: field condition, approach speeds, landing distance, go-around climb gradient • VREF is based on landing weight and flap configuration [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 5: compute landing performance early in the descent to allow time for field condition updates • Consider contaminated runway performance and stopping distance • Verify VREF is consistent with the flap setting planned BOTH

15. Descent RADIO/BARO minimums Set for the approach [FCOM NP.21.38-39:] • Set minimums for the approach type: MDA approach: set BARO to MDA + 50 (or MDA if DA-in-lieu is authorized) • DA approach: set BARO to published DA. CAT II: set RADIO to DH. CAT III: reset (blank) minimums • Both pilots independently verify [FCOM NP.21.38-39:] • For approach with MDA, set BARO to MDA + 50 (FCOM NP.21 Descent Procedure) • Technique: verify minimums independently during descent (not during the approach) to reduce workload on final • Technique: MDA + 50 protects against descending below MDA during a missed approach initiation BOTH

15. Descent NAV RADIO page Set for the approach [FCOM NP.21.38-39:] • PM sets the NAV RADIO page for the approach: tune ILS/GLS frequency and course (or GLS channel), verify navaids tuned and identified, set backup navigation as needed for the specific approach type PM

15. Descent AUTOBRAKE selector Set needed brake setting [FCOM NP.21.38-39:] • PM sets the AUTOBRAKE selector to the needed brake setting • For CAT II/III operations, autobrake must be set to a value that results in a factored landing distance not exceeding the landing distance available • Consider runway length, contamination, and aircraft landing weight [FCTM:] • FCTM 6.21: use of the autobrake system is recommended whenever the runway is limited, when using higher than normal approach speeds, landing on slippery runways, or landing in a crosswind • 3 or 4 for wet or slippery runways or when landing rollout distance is limited; MAX AUTO when minimum stopping distance is required (FCTM 6.21) • Technique: select the setting early so it can be verified during the descent checklist • Do not rely on autobrake alone for stopping on contaminated runways PM

15. Descent FMC arrival crosscheck Both pilots, against the chart [FCOM NP.21.38-39:] • If LNAV or VNAV is used for the arrival/approach, both pilots crosscheck FMC waypoint names, speeds, altitudes, and sequences against the chart • Normally satisfied by both pilots independently verifying • Alternatively, one reads from source material while the other verifies in the FMC (e.g., for late approach changes) • If ORCN segment waypoints differ, repeat independent legs verification [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 5: the FMC arrival crosscheck is a mandatory two-pilot task, not a courtesy • STAR transitions, altitude restrictions, and speed constraints must all match the chart and ATC clearance before loading the approach BOTH

Descent Approach briefing Complete, call DESCENT CHECKLIST [FCOM NP.21.38-39:] • PF briefs the approach • The briefing must include: approach type and procedure, nav frequencies and course, field elevation, MSA, IAF/FAF/MAP, DA/MDA, missed approach procedure, and a reminder that go-arounds on or near the ground require go-around thrust to be set manually and that a flap configuration warning can sound • Then call DESCENT CHECKLIST [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 5: a thorough approach briefing is the key to a safe, unhurried approach • An abbreviated briefing for a repeat approach to the same airport is acceptable but must still cover DA/MDA, missed approach, and any changed conditions ✅ DESCENT CHECKLIST — PF calls, PM reads. (FCOM NP.21.39) [PRC Crew Briefing Card:] • Threats: PM states first, then PF • Plan: Route (STAR / Approach / Approach Mode) · Missed Approach / Fuel / Route to alternate · Landing Runway Assessment / Exit / Taxi · Autobrakes · Flaps + Approach Target Speed • Considerations: any specific PM duties, recap as needed [FCOM NP.21.39:] • Must include reminder: go-arounds on or near the ground require go-around thrust set manually, and a flap configuration warning can sound PF

(FCOM NP.21.41) PF

PF is simultaneously intercepting with appropriate roll mode (LNAV, HDG SEL, etc.), arming APP mode, and verifying localizer capture and final approach course heading [FCTM:] • FCTM 5.9: the ILS/GLS approach flow pattern assumes all approach preparations are complete • TAXI light ON when cleared is an ATC visibility aid and signals to ground crews that the aircraft is inbound [Light Switch Positions card, 27MAR24:] [IMG:lights/cleared_for_approach.jpg] PM

Landing - ILS/GLS APP mode Arm [FCOM NP.21.42:] • When on localizer intercept heading: verify the navigation radios are tuned and identified, and the deviation pointers are shown • Arm the APP mode • When using LNAV to intercept the final approach course, LNAV might parallel the localizer without capturing it • Use LNAV, HDG SEL/TRK SEL or HDG HOLD/TRK HOLD to intercept the final approach course as needed PF

17. Landing - ILS/GLS Gear DOWN, Flaps 20 PF calls at glideslope alive, PM sets [FCOM NP.21.42-50:] • PM calls "LOCALIZER ALIVE" and "GLIDESLOPE ALIVE." At glideslope alive, PF calls "GEAR DOWN, FLAPS 20," PM sets landing gear lever to DN and flap lever to 20 • PF sets speedbrake lever to ARMED [FCTM:] • FCTM 5.9-5.10: ILS or GLS Approach Profile • At glideslope alive the configuration change is sequenced: gear down first (heaviest, most drag), then flaps 20, then arm speedbrake • The glideslope alive callout is the PM trigger for this sequence • At 500 ft AFE verify autoland status if doing an autoland # Autoland: max airport field elevation 8,400 ft (FCOM L.10.8) # Autoland: max headwind 25 kt, max tailwind 15 kt, max crosswind 25 kt (15 kt for CAT II/III) (FCOM L.10.9) # Autoland: glideslope angle 2.5 deg min / 3.25 deg max (FCOM L.10.9) # Without LAND 2 or LAND 3: autopilot must be disengaged below 135 ft AGL (FCOM L.10.8) # With LAND 2 or LAND 3 and glideslope > 3.25 deg: autopilot must be disengaged below 100 ft AGL (FCOM L.10.8) BOTH

Landing - ILS/GLS Speedbrake lever ARMED [FCOM NP.21.42-50:] • PF sets SPEEDBRAKE lever to ARMED after gear down and flaps 20 • Armed speedbrakes auto-extend on touchdown to maximize ground deceleration • Verify the SPEEDBRAKES ARMED memo is shown on EICAS [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 6 Landing: both pilots should monitor automatic speedbrake extension after touchdown • PM announces speedbrake position • If auto-extension fails, manually extend • Pilot awareness of speedbrake position during landing is critical to preventing overruns PF

17. Landing - ILS/GLS Landing flaps PF calls FLAPS ___ at glideslope capture [FCOM NP.21.42-50:] • At glideslope capture, PF calls landing flaps (e.g., "FLAPS 30") • PM sets the flap lever as directed • PF then calls "LANDING CHECKLIST." Checklist: Speedbrake ARMED, Landing gear DOWN, Flaps ___. Verify all three confirmed [FCTM:] • FCTM 5.9-5.10: landing flaps are set at glideslope capture, giving the FMC time to compute the final VREF and allowing for stabilization before 1000 ft AFE. Stabilized approach: on speed, on profile, in configuration, no more than 1000 fpm descent by 1000 ft AFE BOTH

17. Landing - ILS/GLS Missed approach altitude Set on the MCP [FCOM NP.21.42-50:] • PF sets the missed approach altitude on the MCP when at least 300 feet below the missed approach altitude • Setting too early risks altitude capture on the approach - setting too late adds workload on go-around [FCOM NP.21.43:] • FCOM NP.21.43 Landing Procedure: when at least 300 feet below the missed approach altitude, set the missed approach altitude on the MCP; this prevents inadvertent altitude capture while on the approach • FCTM 5.10 uses a different trigger: set the missed approach altitude when established on the glide slope • On a go-around the altitude is already set for the missed approach procedure # Do not use FLCH on final approach below 1,000 ft AFE (FCOM L.10.9) ✅ LANDING CHECKLIST — PF calls, PM reads. (FCOM NP.21.43: call follows setting the missed approach altitude) PF

17. Landing - ILS/GLS NOSE LANDING light ON when cleared to land [FCOM NP.21.42-50:] • PM selects NOSE LANDING light ON when cleared to land • At DA(H): if suitable visual reference is established, PF disengages autopilot in accordance with regulatory requirements (CAT I: by 200 ft, CAT II: at or before alert height, CAT III: as required by approach authorization) and maintains the glide path to landing [FCTM:] • FCTM 5.9-5.10: the decision to continue at DA(H) requires the required visual references specified in the instrument approach procedure • If visual reference is not established, immediately initiate a go-around [Light Switch Positions card, 27MAR24:] [IMG:lights/cleared_to_land.jpg] PM

18. Landing - IAN Initial modes HDG SEL/pitch (vectors) or LNAV/VNAV (to a fix) [FCOM NP.21.45 — Instrument Approach Using IAN:] • If on radar vectors: HDG SEL, pitch mode as needed • If enroute to a fix: LNAV or other roll mode, VNAV or other pitch mode • IAN use requires a published GP angle on the LEGS page, a RWxx waypoint at the runway, or a missed approach waypoint before the runway (e.g., MXxx); not authorized using QFE PF

docs.t: 18. Landing - IAN - Nav radios / deviation pointers
docs.x: 18. Landing - IAN Nav radios / deviation pointers Verify tuned & identified; pointers shown [FCOM NP.21.45:] • When on the localizer/final approach course intercept heading, verify the navigation radios are tuned and identified (as needed) • Verify the deviation pointers are shown PF
18. Landing - IAN TAXI light ON when cleared for the approach [FCOM NP.21.45:] • PM selects the TAXI light switch ON when cleared for the approach PM

18. Landing - IAN APP mode Arm; intercept final approach course [FCOM NP.21.45:] • Arm the APP mode • Use LNAV, HDG SEL, TRK SEL, HDG HOLD, or TRK HOLD to intercept the final approach course as needed • PM calls “COURSE/LOCALIZER ALIVE” • Verify the localizer/final approach course is captured PF

18. Landing - IAN Gear DOWN, Flaps 20 ~2 NM before FAF; PM: APPROACHING GLIDE PATH [FCOM NP.21.45:] • Approximately 2 NM before the final approach fix, PF calls “GEAR DOWN”, “FLAPS 20” • PM calls “APPROACHING GLIDE PATH”, sets the landing gear lever DN, sets the flap lever to 20 BOTH
18. Landing - IAN Speedbrake lever ARMED [FCOM NP.21.45:] • Set the speedbrake lever to ARMED PF
18. Landing - IAN Landing flaps At GP capture PF calls FLAPS___; PM sets [FCOM NP.21.45:] • At glide path capture, PF calls “FLAPS ___” as needed for landing; PM sets the flap lever as directed BOTH

18. Landing - IAN Missed approach altitude Set on the MCP [FCOM NP.21.45:] • Set the missed approach altitude on the MCP • Call “LANDING CHECKLIST”; at the FAF verify the crossing altitude; monitor the approach PF

docs.t: 18. Landing - IAN - NOSE LANDING light / autopilot
docs.x: 18. Landing - IAN NOSE LANDING light / autopilot ON when cleared to land; A/P off at minimums [FCOM NP.21.45:] • PM selects the NOSE LANDING light switch ON when cleared to land • If suitable visual reference is established at DA(H), MDA(H), or the missed approach point, disengage the autopilot per regulatory requirements and maintain the glide path to landing PM

19. Landing - VNAV Initial modes HDG SEL/pitch (vectors) or LNAV/VNAV (to a fix) [FCOM NP.21.48 — Instrument Approach Using VNAV:] • If on radar vectors: HDG SEL, pitch mode as needed • If enroute to a fix: LNAV or other roll mode, VNAV or other pitch mode • Recommended final-approach roll modes: RNAV/GPS/VOR/NDB → LNAV; B/CRS → LNAV or B/CRS; LOC/SDF/LDA/ILS(G/S off)/IGS(G/S off) → LNAV or LOC • VNAV use requires a published GP angle on the LEGS page, an RWxx waypoint at the runway, or a missed approach waypoint before the runway (e.g., MXxx); not authorized using QFE PF

19. Landing - VNAV Localizer (LOC/B/CRS/SDF/LDA) Verify tuned & identified; LOC pointer shown [FCOM NP.21.48:] • When on the final approach course intercept heading for LOC, B/CRS, SDF, or LDA approaches, verify the localizer is tuned and identified and the LOC pointer is shown PF
19. Landing - VNAV TAXI light ON when cleared for the approach [FCOM NP.21.48:] • PM selects the TAXI light switch ON when cleared for the approach PM

docs.t: 19. Landing - VNAV - LNAV or LOC mode
docs.x: 19. Landing - VNAV LNAV or LOC mode Arm; intercept final approach course [FCOM NP.21.48:] • Arm the LNAV or LOC mode • WARNING: when using LNAV to intercept the localizer, LNAV might parallel the localizer without capturing it — the airplane can then descend on the VNAV path with the localizer not captured • Use LNAV, HDG SEL, TRK SEL, HDG HOLD, or TRK HOLD to intercept the final approach course; PM calls “COURSE/LOCALIZER ALIVE”; verify LNAV engaged or the localizer captured PF

docs.t: 19. Landing - VNAV - DA/MDA + VNAV + speed intervention
docs.x: 19. Landing - VNAV DA/MDA + VNAV + speed intervention ~2 NM before FAF, after ALT/VNAV PTH/VNAV ALT [FCOM NP.21.48:] • Approximately 2 NM before the FAF and after ALT, VNAV PTH, or VNAV ALT is annunciated: set DA(H) or MDA(H) on the MCP; select or verify VNAV; select or verify speed intervention • PM calls “APPROACHING GLIDE PATH” PF
19. Landing - VNAV Gear DOWN, Flaps 20 PF calls; PM sets gear DN, flaps 20 [FCOM NP.21.48:] • PF calls “GEAR DOWN”, “FLAPS 20”; PM sets the landing gear lever DN and the flap lever to 20 BOTH
19. Landing - VNAV Speedbrake lever ARMED [FCOM NP.21.48:] • Set the speedbrake lever to ARMED PF

19. Landing - VNAV Landing flaps Beginning final descent PF calls FLAPS___; PM sets [FCOM NP.21.48:] • Beginning the final approach descent, PF calls “FLAPS ___” as needed for landing; PM sets the flap lever as directed BOTH

20. Go-Around GO AROUND / TO/GA PF calls, pushes TO/GA [FCOM NP.21.51:] • PF calls "GO AROUND" and pushes TO/GA switch • WARNING: TO/GA function is inhibited close to the ground and after touchdown • If the thrust levers do not respond when TO/GA is pushed, or if the go-around is initiated after touchdown, manually advance the thrust levers to go-around thrust • A go-around on or near the ground requires manual thrust setting and a flap configuration warning can sound [FCOM NP.21.51:] • FCOM NP.21.51: the "GO AROUND" callout is the trigger for the PM sequence: set the flap lever as directed, verify thrust is sufficient, call "THRUST SET," verify positive rate of climb on the altimeter and call "POSITIVE RATE." The PM does not do anything until hearing the callout • FCTM 5.67 covers the maneuver: push TO/GA, verify thrust increases, call for flaps, rotate smoothly toward 15 degrees pitch • A premature or delayed response by either pilot is a common go-around hazard PF

20. Go-Around FLAPS 20 PF calls, PM sets [FCOM NP.21.51:] • PF calls "FLAPS 20" or "FLAPS ___" as needed • PM sets the flap lever as directed • PM verifies thrust is sufficient for the go-around or adjusts as needed, then calls "THRUST SET." [FCTM:] • All-engine go-around: flaps 20 (or flaps as needed) (FCTM 5.67) • One engine inoperative: flaps 5 from a flaps 20 approach, flaps 20 from a flaps 25 or 30 approach (FCTM 5.70) BOTH

20. Go-Around Gear UP PF calls at positive rate, PM sets [FCOM NP.21.51:] • PF verifies positive rate of climb on the altimeter and calls "GEAR UP." PM verifies positive rate and sets the landing gear lever to UP [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 5: verify positive rate on the altimeter (not just the VSI) before calling gear up • A momentary VSI climb is not sufficient • On very short runways or obstacle-constrained departures, gear retraction timing is critical BOTH

20. Go-Around Roll mode above 400 ft Verify or select; MA altitude set [FCOM NP.21.51:] • Above 400 ft radio altitude, PF verifies or selects a roll mode • Verify that the missed approach altitude is set on the MCP. Verify that the missed approach route is being tracked • The missed approach altitude was set during the approach [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 5: the 400 ft point is the standard transition from pitch-attitude/airspeed control to autopilot and LNAV/VNAV engagement if desired • If the missed approach has a specific turning instruction, it must be flown accurately BOTH

docs.t: 20. Go-Around - Flaps on schedule at accel height
docs.x: 20. Go-Around Flaps on schedule at accel height PF calls, PM sets; FLCH/VNAV [FCOM NP.21.51:] • At acceleration height, PF sets speed to the maneuver speed for the planned flap setting • PF calls flap retractions per the schedule • After flaps are set to the planned setting and at or above the flap maneuvering speed, select FLCH or VNAV as needed • Verify climb thrust is set • Verify missed approach altitude capture • Call AFTER TAKEOFF CHECKLIST [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 5: retract flaps on the published schedule, not early • Retracting too quickly reduces lift margin near the ground • The FCTM cautions that a go-around on or near the ground requires go-around thrust manually, and a flap configuration warning may sound during the go-around if the configuration is not correct ✅ AFTER TAKEOFF CHECKLIST — PF calls, PM reads. (FCOM NP.21.51) BOTH

docs.t: 21. Landing Roll - Thrust levers / SPEEDBRAKE lever
docs.x: 21. Landing Roll Thrust levers / SPEEDBRAKE lever Verify closed / verify UP [FCOM NP.21.52:] • Both pilots verify thrust levers are closed and SPEEDBRAKE lever is UP. PM calls "SPEEDBRAKES UP" or "SPEEDBRAKES NOT UP" if not • Monitor rollout progress and verify correct autobrake operation [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 6: both pilots monitor automatic speedbrake extension after touchdown • PM announces the speedbrake position • If auto-extension fails, manually extend immediately • Fly nose wheels smoothly to the runway - any delay markedly increases stopping distance • The PM speedbrake callout builds habit patterns that prevent failure to observe a malfunctioned speedbrake BOTH

21. Landing Roll Reverse thrust Raise to interlocks without delay, apply as needed [FCOM NP.21.52:] • PF raises reverse thrust levers to the interlocks without delay and holds light pressure until the interlocks release • Apply reverse thrust as needed • WARNING: after the reverse levers are raised, a full stop landing must be made • If an engine remains in reverse, safe flight is not possible • PM calls "REVERSERS NORMAL" when both REV indications are green, or calls out any missing or amber reverser indication [FCTM:] • FCTM 6.17: reverse thrust and speedbrake drag are most effective at high speed • Deploy with as little delay as possible after touchdown • Speedbrakes fully deployed with maximum reverse and maximum manual antiskid braking gives the minimum stopping distance • When stopping is assured and approaching 60 KIAS, start reducing reverse thrust; reverse to idle between 60 KIAS and taxi speed to prevent exhaust re-ingestion and FOD (FCTM 6.26) # Intentional selection of reverse thrust in flight is prohibited (FCOM L.10.10) # Backing the airplane with use of reverse thrust is prohibited (FCOM L.10.10) PF

21. Landing Roll Reverse Idle By 60 KIAS - Reverse to idle detent before taxi speed [FCOM NP.21.52:] • PM calls "60 KNOTS." By 60 kts PF starts movement of the reverse thrust levers to reach the reverse idle detent before taxi speed • After engines at reverse idle, move reverse thrust levers full down [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 6: rudder control is effective to approximately 60 kts - rudder pedal steering is sufficient for maintaining directional control during rollout • Do not use the nose wheel steering tiller until reaching taxi speed • In a crosswind, displace the control wheel into the wind to maintain wings level, which aids directional control PF

21. Landing Roll Autobrake Disarm before taxi speed, manual braking [FCOM NP.21.52:] • PF disarms the autobrake before taxi speed • Use manual braking as needed for the remainder of the rollout and taxi • Autobrake disengages automatically when the pilot applies manual braking or at low speed - manual disarming is procedurally required before the turn-off [FCTM:] • FCTM Ch 6: do not disengage autobrake too early if the runway is short or contaminated • Allow the autobrake to do its job through the high-speed portion of the rollout before transitioning to manual PF

21. Landing Roll Autopilot Disconnect before turning off the runway [FCOM NP.21.52:] • PF disconnects the autopilot before turning off the runway • The autopilot must be disconnected before initiating any turn off the runway to ensure the pilot has direct control of the airplane during the ground maneuvering transition [FCTM:] • FCTM: standard practice to ensure manual control is established for the taxi phase • If a CAT III autoland was performed, the autopilot may be providing rollout guidance - disconnect at an appropriate point before the turn-off PF

22. After Landing SPEEDBRAKE lever DOWN (Captain positions or verifies) [FCOM NP.21.53:] • Captain positions or verifies SPEEDBRAKE lever is DOWN. Start the After Landing Procedure when clear of the active runway • Engine cooldown: run the engines for at least 3 minutes - use a thrust setting no higher than that normally used for all-engine taxi operations [FCOM NP.21.53:] • FCOM NP.21.53 After Landing Procedure: the captain positions or verifies that the SPEEDBRAKE lever is DOWN • Confirmed in Flows Rev 4 (16APR25) as a Captain responsibility CA

22. After Landing APU selector START, then ON, as needed [FCOM NP.21.53:] • PM starts APU (START then ON) as needed • The APU provides electrical power and bleed air for the packs during taxi in • Starting the APU early allows it to stabilize before engine shutdown [FCOM NP.21.53:] • FCOM NP.21.53: the After Landing Procedure starts when clear of the active runway; set the APU selector to START, then ON, as needed • Technique: starting the APU on the runway exit lets both engines shut down promptly at the gate, reducing engine wear time PM

22. After Landing ENGINE ANTI-ICE selectors ON if needed [FCOM NP.21.53:] • PM sets ENGINE ANTI-ICE selectors to ON if icing conditions exist during taxi in • EAI should remain ON in icing conditions until engines are shut down • AUTO mode is not used for EAI during taxi PM

22. After Landing Exterior lights As needed [FCOM NP.21.53:] • PM sets exterior lights as needed • Landing lights are turned off, taxi lights remain on, strobe lights turned off (common courtesy at the gate area) • WING lights off • Specific configuration per company policy and local airport requirements [Light Switch Positions card, 27MAR24:] [IMG:lights/taxi_in.jpg] PM

22. After Landing WX radar / terrain Off [FCOM NP.21.53:] • The pilot flying sets the weather radar (and terrain) to off • Company Flows Rev 4: WX RADAR/TERR — OFF • Engine cooldown: run the engines for at least 3 minutes; thrust no higher than normal all-engine taxi PF

22. After Landing AUTOBRAKE selector OFF [FCOM NP.21.53:] • PM selects AUTOBRAKE OFF. With the airplane on the ground and the landing roll complete, autobrake is no longer needed and the system should be disarmed to prevent inadvertent activation during taxi PM

22. After Landing Flap lever UP [FCOM NP.21.53:] • PM sets flap lever to UP. Retracting the flaps after landing improves fuel efficiency during taxi (reduced drag), prevents contamination from ground water or FOD at taxi speed, and allows the slat/flap mechanism to complete its travel before the next flight [FCOM NP.21.53:] • FCOM NP.21.53 (PM column): flap retraction after landing is a PM (FO) item in the official flow sequence; confirmed in Flows Rev 4 (16APR25) PM

22. After Landing Transponder mode selector XPDR [FCOM NP.21.53:] • PM sets TRANSPONDER MODE selector to XPDR. Changing from TA/RA to XPDR mode disables TCAS resolution advisories (which are not useful on the ground and can cause confusion) while maintaining ATC transponder function for ground surveillance (ADS-B out) PM

22. After Landing COMPANY ARRIVAL REPORT Verify/set ON TIME, IN TIME, LANDING PILOT [FCOM NP.21.53:] • PM verifies or sets the ON TIME, IN TIME, and LANDING PILOT on the COMPANY ARRIVAL REPORT page • NOTE: the ARRIVAL REPORT must be completed before block-in, but does not need to be sent as the data is automatically downlinked at block-in • All three fields are required PM
23. Shutdown Parking brake Set [FCOM NP.21.54:] • Verify that the PARKING BRAKE SET message is shown PF

23. Shutdown Electrical power Set [FCOM NP.21.54:] • If APU power is needed: check the APU RUNNING message is shown • If external power is needed: verify FORWARD EXTERNAL POWER L AVAIL illuminated, push the L switch, verify ON light • If the FORWARD EXTERNAL POWER R AVAIL light is illuminated: push the R switch, verify ON light FO

23. Shutdown FUEL CONTROL switches CUTOFF [FCOM NP.21.54-55:] • CA moves both FUEL CONTROL switches to CUTOFF, shutting down both engines • Procedure preamble (done before this flow step): CA sets parking brake (verify PARKING BRAKE SET message) and FO sets electrical power (APU or external power) • If towing is needed: establish comms, verify nose gear steering locked out • Do not turn the tiller or use brakes during pushback/towing [FCOM NP.21.53:] • FCOM NP.21.53: run the engines for at least 3 minutes before shutdown, thrust no higher than that normally used for all-engine taxi • Background, not manual text: hot section components are susceptible to carbon-coking if shut down immediately after high-power operation CA

23. Shutdown Nose gear steering Verify locked out (if towing) [FCOM NP.21.54:] • If towing is needed: establish communications with ground handling personnel • WARNING: If the nose gear steering is not locked out, any change to hydraulic power with the tow bar connected may cause unwanted tow bar movement • CAUTION: Do not turn the nose wheel tiller during pushback or towing; do not use airplane brakes to stop the airplane during pushback or towing CA
23. Shutdown Parking brake Set or release (if towing) [FCOM NP.21.55:] • Set or release as directed by ground handling personnel BOTH

23. Shutdown SEAT BELTS selector OFF [FCOM NP.21.54-55:] • FO selects SEAT BELTS selector OFF. Turns off the seatbelt sign, signaling to passengers they may deplane • Done after parking brake is set and engines are secure FO

23. Shutdown HYDRAULIC panel All electric pumps OFF [FCOM NP.21.54-55:] • FO sets all electric hydraulic pumps OFF: LEFT ELECTRIC DEMAND OFF, CENTER 1 and CENTER 2 OFF, RIGHT ELECTRIC DEMAND OFF. NOTE: disregard EICAS alerts during PFC self-test after hydraulic shutdown • Wait approximately 3 minutes after HYD PRESS SYS L+C+R message before recording maintenance log entries [FCOM NP.21.55:] • FCOM NP.21.55: disregard EICAS alert and status messages displayed during the PFC self-test after hydraulic shutdown • Premature recording of status messages during this window leads to false maintenance write-ups FO

23. Shutdown FUEL PUMP switches OFF [FCOM NP.21.54-55:] • FO turns all FUEL PUMP switches OFF. With engines shut down the fuel pumps are no longer needed • Turning them off prevents pump wear and eliminates fuel movement through a pressurized system at the gate FO

23. Shutdown BEACON light switch OFF [FCOM NP.21.54-55:] • FO selects BEACON light switch OFF. Rotating beacon OFF signals to ground crews that engines are shut down and it is safe to approach • Never turn the beacon OFF until engines are confirmed shutdown [FCTM:] • FCTM: beacon ON/OFF is the universal signal between flight crew and ground • Beacon ON = engines running or about to start - beacon OFF = safe to approach [Light Switch Positions card, 27MAR24:] [IMG:lights/shutdown.jpg] FO

23. Shutdown FLIGHT DIRECTOR switches OFF (both) [FCOM NP.21.54-55:] • Both CA and FO select FLIGHT DIRECTOR switches OFF. Turns off both FDs at shutdown as a clean state for the next crew • The next crew will configure FDs fresh during preflight [FCTM:] • FCTM: FDs left ON can confuse the next crew during preflight if modes are set from the previous flight BOTH

23. Shutdown TRANSPONDER MODE selector STANDBY [FCOM NP.21.54-55:] • FO sets TRANSPONDER MODE selector to STANDBY. Stops ATC transponder and ADS-B Out transmissions while maintaining system readiness for the next flight • Checklist specifies STANDBY, not OFF [FCTM:] • FCTM: XPDR mode at the gate can confuse ATC ground radar and ADS-B systems • STANDBY is the standard parked state FO

23. Shutdown Status messages Check [FCOM NP.21.54-55:] • FO checks status messages on EICAS. Verify only expected messages after hydraulic shutdown and PFC self-test • Any unexpected status messages require MEL review before next departure • Wait approximately 3 minutes after HYD PRESS SYS L+C+R before recording • Then CA calls SHUTDOWN CHECKLIST; FO does it • If ground conditioned air will be used, accomplish SP.2 FO

23. Shutdown APU selector As needed [FCOM NP.21.55:] • Set the APU selector as needed, then call "SHUTDOWN CHECKLIST" (CA) • Note: If ground conditioned air will be used, accomplish Ground Conditioned Air Use, SP.2 ✅ SHUTDOWN CHECKLIST — CA calls, FO reads. (FCOM NP.21.55) FO

24. Secure IRS selectors OFF [FCOM Flows Rev 4, NP.21:] • FO selects IRS selectors to OFF. Run the Securing Procedure any time the flight deck will be left unattended • The IRS must be OFF before removing all electrical power to prevent damage to the inertial reference units [FCTM:] • FCTM: IRS OFF first in the Securing Procedure prevents alignment mode faults when battery power is removed • The IRS requires a clean power-down sequence FO

24. Secure BATTERY switch Off [FCOM Flows Rev 4, NP.21:] • FO selects BATTERY switch to OFF. CAUTION: the Power Electronics Cooling System (PECS) requires a cool-down period to prevent damaging the units and degrading the coolant • A wait of up to 22 minutes may be required before removing battery power • Verify the PECS cool-down is complete before turning off the battery [FCOM NP.21.56:] • PECS is the liquid cooling system for the high-voltage power electronics (motor controllers), not a battery cooler • Removing power early can damage the liquid-cooled units and degrade the coolant (FCOM NP.21.56 CAUTION) • Cool-down after pack and hydraulic EMP shutdown: 10 min on APU or both forward external power sources, 22 min on a single forward external source (FCOM SP.6.1 Electrical Power Down) • This is a unique 787 characteristic with no A330 equivalent FO

24. Secure FD POWER switch OFF [FCOM Flows Rev 4, NP.21:] • FO selects FLIGHT DECK DOOR POWER switch to OFF. This removes power from the flight deck door access control system • The door will default to the unlocked position when power is removed, allowing normal cabin crew access [FCTM:] • FCTM: FD door power OFF is part of the standard securing sequence • If the flight deck will be left unattended for an extended period, ensure the door is secured per company policy FO

24. Secure EMERGENCY LIGHTS switch OFF [FCOM Flows Rev 4, NP.21:] • FO selects EMERGENCY LIGHTS switch to OFF (guard closed) • With all electrical power removed, this prevents emergency lights from draining any remaining battery power • The switch guard prevents inadvertent activation [FCTM:] • FCTM: do not turn off emergency lights if any personnel remain on board who may need them for egress • The Securing Procedure is only done when the flight deck is left unattended with no remaining passengers FO

24. Secure PACK switches OFF [FCOM Flows Rev 4, NP.21:] • FO selects PACK switches to OFF. With engines and APU shut down, the packs have no air source and can be turned off • This removes power from the air conditioning control units [FCTM:] • FCTM: packs OFF completes the air conditioning system shutdown • If ground conditioned air is connected, the packs will have been off since the Ground Conditioned Air Use procedure (SP.2) FO

24. Secure EFB PWR switch Off [FCOM Flows Rev 4, NP.21:] • Both pilots turn their EFB power switches OFF. The EFB is the Electronic Flight Bag containing Jeppesen charts, performance software, and company documents • Both pilots turn off their individual EFBs before leaving the flight deck [FCTM:] • FCTM: EFBs consume battery power if left on • Some EFB configurations have a charging cradle that can drain the airplane battery if left connected • Turn off and stow properly per company EFB procedures BOTH

24. Secure HUD combiner Stow [FCOM Flows Rev 4, NP.21:] • Both pilots stow their HUD combiners • The HUD combiner is the transparent display unit that folds down for flight and stows up for taxi and ground operations • Stowing prevents damage from inadvertent contact during cleaning or maintenance [FCOM NP.21.56:] • FCOM NP.21.56: to prevent the possibility of injury, ensure the combiner is fully raised and securely latched in the stowed position • Verify the HUD is in the stowed position as a condition check for the next crew during the Preliminary Preflight ✅ SECURE CHECKLIST — CA calls, FO reads, both verify. Checklist complete when all items green on the ECL. (QRH CI.1) BOTH
